verdict_word: Adj. EPS edged past; profit missed LSEG, output guide raised
takeaways: Net income rose 21.5% to R$39.75 billion (US$7.74 billion), short of the R$47.02 billion LSEG consensus cited by Reuters; adjusted EPS was $1.44 per AP.
Excluding one-off items (court contingencies, a crude/diesel export tax, asset sales) net income was R$47.9 billion, up 68% year over year.
Production averaged 2.83 million barrels a day, a third straight record, and the 2026 output target rose to 2.7-2.8 million from 2.5 million.
Brent averaged $97 a barrel in the quarter, up more than 40% from a year earlier, lifting revenue 32.4% to R$169.35 billion.
The board approved R$15.3 billion in shareholder payouts tied to the quarter; net debt fell 4.2% to US$57.8 billion.
verdict: Petrobras pumped a record amount of oil at $97 Brent and still came in light on headline profit, because Brazil's tax man and the courts took their cut. The pumps are fine; the paperwork is the problem.
